what_it_does: The model's score for a sentence is the sum of its probabilities for these grades (2 planned, 3 committed): loose first, tightened by the floors.
how_to_tune: Leave unless the scale changes.

what_it_does: The most items (sentences, paragraphs, packages) asked in one request. 0 = one a request. $WBG_ASK_BATCH overrides it.
how_to_tune: Tested 2026-10-22: batches of 10 and of 62 to 66 ranked graded sentences as well as one a request, but moved first answers (1 in 10 crossed 0.5); stored answers never move. Above 120 was never measured. One a request costs about four times as much for measures.

what_it_does: A request holds items up to about this many characters.
how_to_tune: Tested on asset paragraphs 2026-10-22: 80,000 agreed with 30,000 as often.

what_it_does: The starting gate: an asset's question goes to a sentence when the sentence scores at least this against the asset's search phrases or a word pattern of the asset matches (inputs/taxonomy/assets_patterns.csv), until the skip rule (skip.max_loss) has fitted the asset's own gate from graded sentences; the feedback rounds then look below it, as for measures. 0 asks every asset of every sentence and ignores fitted gates.
how_to_tune: A starting value only; the fitted gate replaces it. 0.3 (2026-10-22), the measures' value: the asset map now has the measures' second look below the gate (feedback rounds, and word patterns once the file exists). Raising it later asks nothing; lowering it asks only the sentences it adds.

what_it_does: A sentence has an asset of its own when that asset's posterior reaches this (level unit; every such asset with asset.multiple). Also what counts as a yes in the asset feedback rounds.
how_to_tune: Tested 2026-10-22 with decay 0.4: 0.3 best. ./wbg check all --evaluate writes data/reports/tune.md, which compares floor, paragraph floor and decay on the grades.

what_it_does: A sentence with no asset of its own adds up, for each asset, its own score and every earlier sentence's in its paragraph, each multiplied by this per sentence back (one back x0.4, two back x0.16); every asset whose sum reaches asset.paragraph_floor takes it (the highest only without asset.multiple). 0 turns the rule off.
how_to_tune: Tested on the graded sentences 2026-10-22: 0.4 best of 0 to 1.

what_it_does: A sentence with no asset of its own takes the asset with the highest decayed sum over its paragraph (asset.decay) when that sum reaches this (level paragraph). Its own line because a sum of several scores is on another scale than one sentence's posterior.
how_to_tune: Starts at asset.floor's value (2026-10-22), so nothing moves until it is tuned; the tuning report compares it on the grades.

what_it_does: A sentence has every asset whose posterior reaches asset.floor (or, at level paragraph, every asset whose decayed sum reaches asset.paragraph_floor), best first; false = the best one only. Each asset is its own question, as each measure is.
how_to_tune: true from 2026-10-22: a sentence about a backbone and a data centre names both. The tuning report compares agreement and further assets given on the grades; the asset sheet should let a person give several.

what_it_does: The starting gate: a sentence goes to a measure's question when its best similarity to the measure's phrases and definition reaches this, or a word pattern matches, until the skip rule (skip.max_loss) has fitted the measure's own gate from graded sentences. 0 asks every sentence and ignores fitted gates, as for assets.
how_to_tune: A starting value only; the fitted gate replaces it. 0.3 (2026-10-22): of the commitments the earlier runs found in feedback rounds below the old gate, all but 3 sat at a paragraph best of 0.30 to 0.35 or more; about two in five sentences reach 0.3 for a broad measure, one in ten to twenty for a narrow one. Raising it later asks nothing (the answers are stored); lowering it asks only the sentences it adds.

what_it_does: Also send the measure's best N sentences by similarity, whatever their score. 0 = off.
how_to_tune: Usually off.

what_it_does: The skip rule: each label's gate is the highest cosine that loses at most this share of the sentences a person graded yes under the current question (at their design weights); word-pattern matches are always asked. Fitted by ./wbg check <set> --evaluate, read by the next run.
A label needs at least this many graded yes before its gate is fitted; until then the starting gate above applies.
Sentences sent per relevance-feedback round, per measure (the ones nearest the measure's committed sentences).
A measure whose round finds fewer committed sentences than this stops.
At most this many feedback rounds. 0 turns them off.
How much of the rejected sentences' average is subtracted when choosing the next round.
how_to_tune: 0.5 because the first run's plain centroid pulled in the measure's general neighbourhood. Textbook relevance feedback uses about 0.2 with the original query kept; this one has no query term. Not set from grades: the elusion sheet shows what the rounds miss.

what_it_does: The asset map's own rounds, apart from the measures': sentences sent per round, per asset (the ones nearest the asset's sentences at asset.floor or more).
how_to_tune: Starts at the measures' value. Not set from grades: an elusion sheet on the asset map shows what the rounds miss.

what_it_does: An asset whose round finds fewer sentences at asset.floor than this stops.
At most this many rounds per asset. 0 turns the asset map's rounds off (the gate and word patterns alone).
how_to_tune: An option to compare, not a settled choice: run the asset map with 0 and with 6 (the answers are stored, so only the sentences the rounds add cost anything) and compare the assets found.

what_it_does: How much of the average of the sentences asked and not at asset.floor is subtracted when choosing the next round.
After each model answer, combine the model's score with how similar the sentence is to the sentences a person graded for the same label (src/posterior.py). Off = the model's score alone.
How sharply similarity counts in the weighted vote of graded sentences: higher = only the closest count.
how_to_tune: Tested 2026-10-22: 10 to 20 best of 2 to 160 (on an earlier sheet). ./wbg check all --evaluate writes data/reports/tune.md, which compares settings on the grades (5 to 80).

what_it_does: Also use similarity to the average graded commitment minus similarity to the average graded non-commitment.
how_to_tune: ./wbg check all --evaluate writes data/reports/tune.md, which compares settings on the grades (on, off).

what_it_does: Fit each decision's labels together: the measures in one fit, the assets in one, and likewise the types, the pair checks, the package assets and the package links. Each label keeps its own intercept (its base rate) and its own graded sentences for the vote; the weights on the score and the similarities are shared. false = each label fits its own four weights.
how_to_tune: true from 2026-10-22, for every decision alike: a measure has about 40 graded rows and a type, pair side or asset fewer, few for four weights of its own. ./wbg check all --evaluate writes data/reports/tune.md, which compares pooled and per label on the measures' grades.

what_it_does: How strongly the layer's weights are pulled towards zero: the precision of a normal prior on each standardised weight (1 = a prior standard deviation of 1, 4 = 0.5). More = closer to the model's score alone.
how_to_tune: ./wbg check all --evaluate writes data/reports/tune.md, which compares settings on the grades (0.25, 1, 4).

what_it_does: A label with fewer graded sentences than this (or fewer than posterior.min_each of either kind) gets no layer: its score is the model's.
A label needs at least this many graded yes and this many graded no for a layer.

Leave out of the vote the graded sentences a sentence nearly copies (embedding similarity at this or more), in fitting, checking and applying alike. off = every graded sentence votes but the sentence itself, near-copies and the same project included.
how_to_tune: Off (2026-10-22): word-for-word copies are already merged, only 6 of 1,383 committed sentences had a neighbour in another project above 0.95, and a sentence whose graded near-copy is yes usually is yes. ./wbg check all --evaluate writes data/reports/tune.md, which compares settings on the grades (off, 0.97, 0.95).

A type counts for a committed sentence when its score (P(yes) of the type's fit question, yes, unsure or no, told the sentence is already committed; through the types' layer once fitted, src/judged.py) reaches this; with types.multiple every such type, best first. None reaching it = no type.
how_to_tune: 0.5, the floor every decision starts at. On 43 committed risk-assessment sentences and 7 draft types (2026-10-22): 1.8 types a sentence at 0.5, 1.3 at 0.7 (one choice had given 1). Set from data/reports/evaluate_after_measures.md once the type column of graded sheets is filled.

what_it_does: Every type at floor.types counts, not only the likeliest. false = the likeliest only.
how_to_tune: The types are written to exclude each other, so a second type that often counts means two definitions overlap: fix the wording.

what_it_does: A measure proposes new (OTH) types only from at least this many committed sentences no approved type counts for.
how_to_tune: Fewer are reported, not proposed from.

what_it_does: A sentence two measures both commit stays in a measure when that side's posterior (P(yes) of the fit question: does the measure apply, the other measure's boundary beside it; through the measure's pair layer once fitted) reaches this.
how_to_tune: 0.5, the floor every decision starts at (2026-10-22, when the pair check became a fit question per side). Set from the pair checks tab: evaluate_after_measures.md suggests a floor.

what_it_does: Assets asked of each procurement package: its best this many by similarity.

A package has an asset when its posterior (P(yes) of the fit question: does the package buy, build, install, connect, operate or design the asset; through the package-asset layer once fitted, src/judged.py) reaches this.
how_to_tune: Set from the package assets tab: ./wbg check all --evaluate suggests a floor in evaluate_after_measures.md.

what_it_does: Each committed sentence is also paired with its project's nearest this many packages by similarity to the measure.
A further floor on a sentence's posterior probability over every measure for it to count on the dashboards.
Where a commitment's asset may come from: unit (the sentence names it), paragraph (earlier sentences of its paragraph do, their scores summed with asset.decay).
Only Investment Project Financing operations count.

A package counts as linked to a commitment when the link's posterior (P(yes) of the fit question: would carrying out the package deliver the commitment; through the link layer once fitted, src/judged.py) reaches this.
how_to_tune: On the graded sheet (2026-10-21, 70 pairs): from 0.7 up, 25 yes of 26. evaluate_after_measures.md suggests it again from the package links tab.

Words per run when comparing wording: template_share on each search unit and the dashboards' same-wording-across-projects test both cut text into runs of this many words.
how_to_tune: Six since 2026-10-19; not set from grades. Raising it counts only longer shared runs as the same wording.

what_it_does: A sentence two measures both commit leaves a measure the pair check says it is not.
The most one requested measure may spend on models; a run that reaches it stops and resumes from the stored answers the next time the queue runs.
how_to_tune: At the 0.3 starting gate a new measure asks one to four in ten sentences, about US$0.3 to 0.8 on the current corpus, so it usually finishes in one run of the queue.

what_it_does: The most all requested measures together may spend in a UTC day.
